items.titleEn: Gold plunges below $3,750, silver tumbles as hawkish Fed minutes pressure metals - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in late U.S. trading Wednesday, extending their recent losses as a stronger U.S. dollar, expectations for further Federal Reserve interest rate increases and broad commodity-market selling weighed on precious metals. Gold dropped to its lowest level since September 2025, breaking below $3,750.00 an ounce, while silver suffered even heavier losses as concerns about industrial demand and tighter financial conditions compounded the selling. The release of hawkish minutes from the Fed's October meeting reinforced expectations for additional monetary tightening, while renewed U.S.-Iran military tensions failed to generate meaningful safe-haven demand. Spot gold was trading near $3,722.60 an ounce, down $125.90, or 3.27%, while silver was trading near $44.930 an ounce, down $2.340, or 4.95%, on the session. Gold traded as low as $3,719.10 during the day, while silver touched $44.640. Wednesday's U.S. economic data highlighted growing weakness in the housing market despite a rebound in residential construction. October housing starts increased 9.9% to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.309 million units, exceeding expectations for 1.25 million. However, building permits declined 7.4% to 1.295 million units, substantially below expectations for 1.38 million, suggesting weaker construction activity ahead. Pending home sales fell 4.7% in October, considerably worse than expectations for a 2.0% decline, reaching their lowest level since the series began in 2001. Contract signings were 16.7% lower than a year earlier, reflecting the impact of elevated mortgage rates on residential demand. The reports followed Tuesday's figures showing retail sales increased just 0.2% and industrial production declined 0.4% in October. The combination of deteriorating housing demand, slower industrial activity and persistent inflation highlighted the increasingly difficult policy environment facing the Federal Reserve.

items.titleEn: Anthropic IPO prices at $83 a share as ANT prepares Thursday debut
items.summaryEn: Buy ANT (Anthropic) at/near the open. $83 is above the filed range and signals strong institutional demand; the stock should keep catching bids as allocations convert into public float and as AI “new issue” flows chase momentum. Upside is reinforced if the deal is upsized and if index-inclusion timelines (MSCI/FTSE) pull forward passive demand. Key Risk: Demand fades immediately after pricing and the stock gaps down as early buyers realize the valuation is already fully priced. Sell/short the nearest AI IPO/AI infrastructure “hot” names that are most likely to be crowded out by ANT’s attention—e.g., short SOFI? (not AI) better: short NVDA? No. Use a cleaner proxy: sell/short ARKQ (AI ETF) or AI-focused baskets (e.g., BOTZ) into ANT’s first-day strength because capital rotates from other AI exposures into the new high-profile listing, pressuring relative performance for days.

items.titleEn: Gold prices remain under pressure as Fed minutes show central bank committed to cooling inflation
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices have dropped to session lows as the Federal Reserve remains firmly committed to raising interest rates to bring inflation down to its 2% target, according to the latest minutes of the central bank’s monetary policy meeting. Although the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged in October, the minutes showed that committee members see cooling persistent inflation as their top priority. “Most participants expected inflation to remain elevated in the near term but to decline over time toward 2 percent, reflecting the waning of tariff-related price effects, a reduction in energy prices’ contribution to inflation, and a moderation of the pressures associated with the AI buildout. The vast majority saw upside risks to this outlook, citing higher energy prices and continued supply constraints with regard to refined fuel products,” the minutes said.
